subject.title: [Feature]: Add gateway-side circuit breaker for unhealthy sessions after consecutive failures

question: What core session-health breaker contract should OpenClaw own for unhealthy persistent sessions: a unified receipt/state model, a narrow no-progress counter, or deferral to narrower guard tracks?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the requested behavior crosses failure taxonomy, config defaults, persisted session state, retry admission, recovery actions, and operator/UI surfacing, which code inspection cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design unified session-health receipts
options.body: Define a first-class receipt with failure signature, counters, last success, retry admission, suggested recovery, persistence, and operator recovery semantics before implementation.

options.title: Land a narrow no-progress breaker
options.body: Limit the first change to a bounded consecutive no-progress counter in the embedded run loop and explicitly leave UI receipts, persistence, cooldowns, and auto-rotation as follow-up work.

options.title: Defer to narrower guards
options.body: Keep idle-timeout, tool-loop, compaction, provider, cron, and subagent guard tracks separate and later close or narrow this umbrella request.

recommendation.title: Design unified session-health receipts
recommendation.body: Define a first-class receipt with failure signature, counters, last success, retry admission, suggested recovery, persistence, and operator recovery semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the best available routing candidate from current history and adjacent idle-timeout breaker merge history.
